review.scope: Self-authored toy Alloy fixtures through the isolated production worker, local pinned pretrained E5 encoder, and production exact score function. No corpus records were read or modified.
non_claims: This does not measure general semantic retrieval quality.
A finite sample or high similarity is not an equivalence proof.
These fixtures are not held-out dataset evaluation or promotion evidence.

runtime.worker: production isolated namespace worker via allow_retrieval.corpus.worker; each fixture returned FULL with three validated members per polarity
runtime.encoder: pinned local intfloat/e5-base-v2 ONNX encoder, pretrained-only identity adapter; no network calls

checks.details: All four hand-authored fixtures returned FULL; positive and negative existence were SAT, enumeration CAP_REACHED at 3, and each polarity had 3 members. The fixtures include a fact-constrained model, exercising SAT for F AND NOT P.

The checked structural simplification candidate ranked ahead of the opposite-polarity candidate under frozen default weights. Their compatible contexts and canonical witness pools were equal in this fixture, so both pool-overlap terms were 1.
The added-signature/fact candidate was marked INCOMPATIBLE_CONTEXT and received zero positive and negative overlap despite full pools.

score_components.interpretation: In this tiny fixture the E5 canonical similarities are all close to 1; the observed ranking separation comes from exact pool overlap and context gating. This is not evidence of broad semantic discrimination.

exercised: wrong-polarity distinction with a worker-generated opposite predicate
SAT positive and negative pools, including a fact-constrained source
full finite-pool admission at N=3 without treating that status as an equivalence proof
actual local pretrained embedding, frozen weighted score, and ranking
not_exercised: explicit translator instrumentation proving F is passed exactly once, plus an inconsistent-facts UNSAT case
constructed unsampled counterexample demonstrating finite-pool incompleteness
three-root family alias union and split-manifest rejection
checked-rewrite versus semantic-judgment label separation and bad-certificate rejection
zero-overlap sampling-bias rate across a corpus
ANN candidate omission compared with exact top-k
model-wide training-lineage revocation and outbox recovery
blinded human ranking judgments and held-out metric suite
